name: Easy!Appointments
summary: Easy!Appointments 1.6, a self-hosted appointment booking page, with Caddy, PHP 8.3 and MariaDB. Optional domain with HTTPS.
getting_started: Open /index.php/login at your server address and sign in with the user name and password shown once. The user name is admin and your email address is set on the account. The login is also stored on the server in /root/.beltoft-app/credentials.json. The server address without a path is the booking page your customers use. The install adds one service called Service and no provider: under Services rename or change the service, then under Users add yourself as a provider with working hours and the service, or nobody can book. Add a domain for HTTPS before real use; without a domain the address is not encrypted. Booking emails need an SMTP service: outgoing mail on port 25 is blocked on all servers, so use an SMTP service on port 587 or 465, for example our email, Amazon SES or Postmark. Set it in /opt/easyappointments/application/config/email.php: change protocol to 'smtp' and set smtp_host, smtp_user, smtp_pass, smtp_crypto ('tls' for port 587, 'ssl' for port 465), smtp_port, from_name and from_address. The language is English. Danish is included: set LANGUAGE to 'danish' in /opt/easyappointments/config.php, or choose the language in your own account. If the server address or domain changes, set BASE_URL in the same file, because links in emails use it. The web root /var/www/easyappointments holds only index.php and the assets folder. The program files, config.php and your data (the storage folder, with uploads, logs and backups) are in /opt/easyappointments, outside the web root, so database backups and sessions cannot be downloaded. Backups are your job: run runuser -u www-data -- php /var/www/easyappointments/index.php console backup to write a database dump into /opt/easyappointments/storage/backups, and copy that folder and the uploads folder off the server. Updates are manual: as root run easyappointments-update VERSION, for example easyappointments-update 1.6.2, with a version from github.com/alextselegidis/easyappointments/releases. It downloads that release, checks it against the sha256 that GitHub publishes (or one you pass as the second argument), makes a database dump and a copy of the program files in /var/backups/easyappointments, replaces program files only, runs the database migration, checks the booking page and puts everything back by itself if a step fails. easyappointments-rollback restores the last backup, and the database goes back with it. config.php, the storage folder and email.php are kept only when you update this way: do not copy a new release over /opt/easyappointments by hand. Calendar sync runs hourly and clean-up nightly from cron. Easy!Appointments is licensed under the GPL-3.0. The smallest plan runs it for a small business; MariaDB and PHP use about 0.5 GB of memory with few visitors, so choose more memory if many people book at the same time.
